label: Northern Virginia
subtitle: Grid-Stressed · World's Largest DC Market
sources: EPA eGRID2023 Summary Tables rev2 (Tables 1-2, SRVC); EIA-861 2024 Sales_Ult_Cust (Virginia Electric & Power Co, VA); EIA Virginia Electricity Profile 2024; Dominion Energy Virginia 2025 IRP Update; JLARC Report 598 'Data Centers in Virginia' (Dec 2024) and landing page; Loudoun County BOS 'Data Center Capital of the World' strategy paper (2025, ArchiveCenter Item 13979); Loudoun County FY2026 Proposed Budget 'General Fund Revenue and Trends'; Loudoun County web pages /6405, /6407, /6409; Loudoun County Zoning Ordinance 2023 Chapter 4 Sec. 4.06.02; EESI 'Data Centers and Water Consumption'; VPM 2025-12-17 (PEC generator count); InsideNova 2026 (DCD-reported $4.4M/acre offers); LoudounNow Feb 2025 (Commissioner of the Revenue assessment); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 annual normals USW00093738; U.S. Drought Monitor county statistics API (Loudoun 51107); Census ACS 2020-2024 5-yr via Census Reporter API (B01001, B01003, B17001; TIGER 2023 land area); USDA NASS 2022 Census of Agriculture county profile Loudoun; USDA NASS Land Values 2025 Summary; Virginia SLEAC Loudoun use-value brochure (2026 estimates); CDM Smith Trap Rock WTF project page; 40 CFR 63.6640(f) via LII.; v4 rows: US EPA AirData, Annual Summary by Monitor 2024, site 51-107-1005 Broad Run High School, Ashburn, Loudoun County VA, parameter 88101, POC 3, PM25 Annual 2024 sta; U.S. EPA, eGRID2023 Summary Tables rev2 (June 2025), Table 1 'Subregion Output Emission Rates' (total output rate, lb/MWh x 0.4536 = g/kWh); U.S. EPA AVERT v4.3, 2023 avoided PM2.5 emission rates by region (onshore wind, lb/MWh x 0.4536 = g/kWh); U.S. EPA, eGRID2023 Summary Tables rev2 (June 2025), Table 2 'Subregion Resource Mix' (fractions of net generation; oil and other fossil folded into gas); USDA NASS, 2022 Census of Agriculture, Volume 1 Chapter 2 County Level Data, Virginia, Table 25 Field Crops: 2022 and 2017 (st51_2_025_025.pdf) and Table 26 Fie
description: World's largest data center market. Loudoun County alone has about 250 built data centers (~53M sq ft permitted), 117 more in the development pipeline, and 5.33 GW of data-center power consumption in 2025 (county BOS strategy paper). Dominion Energy Virginia's generation portfolio is 20,571 MW (2025 IRP Update) and the PJM DOM zone set a 24,678 MW record peak in January 2025; Dominion holds 16,913 MW of firm data-center contracts. eGRID2023 SRVC grid: 0.270 kg CO2e/kWh, 10% renewables (39.9% nuclear). JLARC (2024) estimates Dominion residential bills rising $14-$37/month by 2040 from data-center-driven generation and transmission; the sales-tax exemption saved the industry $928.6M in FY23. Loudoun expects ~$1.3B in data-center property taxes in FY2027 (38% of General Fund); DC-zoned land trades at $2-6M/acre vs $300-500k/acre otherwise. ~4,700 diesel backup generators in Loudoun; 2023 Loudoun data-center water use ~900M gallons with 'just over a third' of Virginia's DC water from reclaimed sources. Loudoun's 2023 Zoning Ordinance requires 200-ft structure setbacks from residential property and a 55 dBA property-line limit; by-right data centers ended March 2025.
recommendedReason: Water (basin-stress contribution, WUE warning) and the grid-attributable health burden lead the corrected profile; the market's grid share is small against Dominion's 20.6 GW. Procured renewables remove most of the Scope 2 and grid-attributable damages, Tier IV generators address the Title V NOx exceedance, and recycled water cuts freshwater withdrawal from the Potomac basin.

label: Tucson, Arizona
subtitle: Water-Scarce · Desert Climate
sources: Pima County Project Blue FAQ (pima.gov/3552); Pima County Administrator memo 'Update on Project Blue' 17 Sep 2025; TEP Form 10-K FY2025 (SEC); EPA eGRID2023 rev2 summary tables; EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A (June 2026) and Arizona State Electricity Profile 2024; AZPM 28 May 2026 (ADWR well permits); KOLD 25 Apr 2026; Tucson Sentinel 24 Dec 2025; Baxtel Tucson market; NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 normals (USW00023160); USGS 3DEP EPQS; FEMA NFHL and National Risk Index (Pima County); US Drought Monitor county statistics 2000-2026; Census ACS 2019-2023 5-yr tract tables B01003/B01001/B17001 + 2024 Gazetteer; NOAA/NCICS Arizona State Climate Summary; USGS SIR 2025-5017 (SHARP recharge); WRRC Pima County water factsheet (Jan 2024); v4 rows: U.S. EPA AirData, Annual Summary Data by Monitor, 2025 (annual_conc_by_monitor_2025.zip), Pima County AZ (04-019), parameter 88101 PM2.5, pollutant standard 'PM; U.S. EPA, eGRID2023 Summary Tables rev2 (June 2025), Table 1 'Subregion Output Emission Rates' (total output rate, lb/MWh x 0.4536 = g/kWh); U.S. EPA AVERT v4.3, 2023 avoided PM2.5 emission rates by region (onshore wind, lb/MWh x 0.4536 = g/kWh); U.S. EPA, eGRID2023 Summary Tables rev2 (June 2025), Table 2 'Subregion Resource Mix' (fractions of net generation; oil and other fossil folded into gas)
description: Pima County approved Project Blue 3-2 in June 2025 (290 acres north of the Pima County Fairgrounds, west of Houghton Rd); Tucson's City Council rejected annexation and reclaimed-water service in Aug 2025, so developer Beale Infrastructure switched to a closed-loop air-cooled design with no industrial water use and two on-site wells permitted by ADWR for 96.5 acre-feet/yr (~31 M gal/yr; 15,000-20,000 gal/day expected). TEP's ACC-approved Energy Supply Agreement supplies 286 MW from existing capacity; land sold for ~$21 M on 24 Dec 2025; construction began 24 Apr 2026 with up to 10 buildings, 3,000+ construction jobs, 180 permanent jobs and $250 M in taxes over 10 years. Pima County sits in a chronically drought-affected, high-heat, high-wildfire-risk region (FEMA NRI); the AZNM grid runs at 0.32 kg CO2e/kWh with 22% renewables.
recommendedReason: Regional water stress (WRI high) is the constraint, but the approved air-cooled design already minimises direct use, so the remaining water lever is off-site: procured renewables cut the thermoelectric water and grid-attributable health burden of the AZNM supply. Liquid cooling and recycled water matter only if the June-2025 evaporative design returns; high-albedo surfaces reduce cooling demand in desert heat.

description: Jerome Township (Union County) trustees voted 3 Sept 2025 for a nine-month moratorium on new data centers, Ohio's first, after noise complaints about Amazon's two existing campuses; in March 2026 they moved data centers to conditional use. Amazon's facilities hold 100% 10-year county abatements with PILOT donations and paid $1.1M county property tax in 2024. The 98-acre Industrial Parkway campus draws Marysville municipal water (reservoir + wells; the two Amazon sites take ~10% of the city's daily supply, 350,000 gal on a peak day). Union County soils are Class II (prime when drained), 89% of farmland is cropland, soybeans dominate; NASS 2025 Ohio cropland is $9,750/acre while data-center-ready land in New Albany sold at ~$741,000/acre. AEP Ohio: 600 MW data-center load in 2024, 17,861 MW contracted, 5 GW forecast by 2030; grid is eGRID RFCW (0.416 kg CO2e/kWh, 7.6% renewable, 28.4% nuclear).
recommendedReason: Farmland loss cannot be mitigated by technology, but generator upgrades and waste heat recovery improve community acceptance. Extended lifespan and reuse reduce e-waste on productive land.

description: xAI Colossus 1 (Pidgeon Industrial Park, South Memphis): ~250 MW IT / 200,000+ Hopper GPUs built in 122 days on a 522-acre EDGE lease at the former Electrolux plant. Grid: 150 MW TVA supply via a $24 M developer-funded substation (energized 2025) plus Megapacks; MLGW buys all power from TVA (eGRID SRTV 0.41 kg CO2e/kWh, 9 % renewable, 33 % nuclear). On-site generation: 35 unpermitted gas turbines (420+ MW; SELC est. 1,000-2,100 t NOx/yr) ran 2024-25; Shelby County Health Dept. permitted 15 Solar SMT-130 turbines (247 MW, SCR, 87 t NOx/yr PTE) on 2 Jul 2025, under appeal by SELC/NAACP. recommendedReason: The permitted state (15 SCR-equipped turbines, 110 h/yr) removes most of the 2024-25 local NOx burden; the remaining health burden is the TVA grid supply, which procured renewables and grid-supplied power address. Waste heat recovery and high-albedo surfaces offset the South Memphis community and heat burden.

description: Nordic best-case reference anchored on Meta's Luleå, Sweden campus (Porsön, Norrbotten, SE1): three LEED Gold buildings opened 2013-2021, 267,471 MWh/yr metered use at PUE 1.09 (about 28 MW average IT), outside-air cooling with 25.4 ML/yr water (WUE ~0.1 L/kWh), backup generators cut by more than 70% on 2N feeds from a hydro grid with no HV outage since 1979. SE1 is ~97% hydro+wind (8.1 GW installed); Sweden's grid averaged ~35 gCO2/kWh in 2024 (Ember). 300+ permanent staff; Sweden abolished the data-centre electricity-tax rebate on 1 July 2023 (full rate 36 öre/kWh in 2026). Waste-heat capture at Luleå is limited to office heating; the 30% heat-recovery value reflects the Nordic best case (Meta Odense, 215,000 MWh/yr to Fjernvarme Fyn). Reuse rate 83% is Microsoft's Amsterdam Circular Center figure, kept as an assumption.
recommendedReason: Already near-optimal on energy and water. Focus on lifecycle: waste heat district heating generates revenue, 90% reuse closes the loop, extended lifespan reduces embodied carbon further.

description: Oracle/OpenAI 'Stargate Michigan' campus by Related Digital in Saline Township, Washtenaw County: 1,383 MW DTE Electric special contract (MPSC Case U-21990, conditionally approved 18 Dec 2025 with 19-yr term, 80% minimum bill and a developer-funded 1,383 MW storage agreement; Michigan AG sought reconsideration), three 550,000 sq ft buildings on 250 developed acres of a 575-acre A-1 farmland parcel (750 acres protected). Township denied rezoning 4-1 (Sept 2025); developer sued; consent judgment (Oct 2025) caps sound at 55 dB at all property lines, bans high-water-use evaporative cooling, sets 75-ft building setbacks, bars expansion and funds $4M farmland trust, $2M community fund and fire services. Closed-loop air-cooled design using ~20,000 gal/day from an on-site well (EGLE Site-Specific Review 681 gpm, 100% return flow to the Saline River, no adverse resource impact, Apr 2026). EGLE air permit PTI0000135 (13 Jan 2026): 14 diesel emergency generators + 1 fire pump, 34.86 tpy NOx potential. 2,500 union construction jobs, 450+ on-site permanent jobs; 12-year 50% PA 198 abatement approved Jul 2026 on a $4.8B basis (<$20M/yr) rather than the $43B current valuation. DTE calculates ~$300M net benefit to other customers; grid mix eGRID RFCM 0.443 kg CO2e/kWh, 11% renewable.
recommendedReason: At 1.4 GW scale, even small % improvements are massive in absolute terms. 90% renewables on 1.12 GW IT load saves millions of tonnes CO₂. Waste heat recovery at this scale could heat a small city.
